title: Approaching Jesus versus approaching to betray him
english: "Look, the one who will betray me has drawn near" (Matthew 26:46). Drawing near to Jesus is not the same thing as drawing near for the purpose of betraying him. The betrayer had withdrawn himself from Jesus by sins, and by the betrayal he had planned to carry out against him; he drew near to hand over the Son of God, whom he had already betrayed. All transgressors first betray Jesus, and afterward they hand him over.
translator_notes: Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Origen is commenting on Jesus' words in Gethsemane, 'Behold, the one who betrays me has drawn near,' and distinguishes two kinds of approaching Jesus.

title: Judas arrives with the armed crowd
english: While he was still speaking, Judas, one of the twelve, came, and with him a large crowd with swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests (Matthew 26:47). They feared that because of the multitude of believers he might be seized; but I think they supposed he could escape by magical arts. Glory to Christ. Amen.
translator_notes: Series rem arrest from PG 13 Latin.
orientation: Origen is commenting on Matthew 26:47, where Judas arrives with a crowd while Jesus is still speaking.
